extracted.intended_audience: prospective U.S. patent applicants (independent inventors, small businesses, and practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for deciding whether to seek a U.S. patent, searching prior art, preparing and filing a complete application with the USPTO (Patent Center/eFiler), prosecuting the application with an examiner, and receiving and maintaining the issued patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether a patent is appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide if a patent is right for you: a U.S. patent gives the owner the right to exclude others from making, using, offering for sale, selling throughout, or importing an invention into the U.S. for a limited time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which type of patent (utility for new and useful machines/processes/compositions/articles of manufacture; design for new, original, ornamental designs; plant patents for asexually reproduced distinct new plant varieties). If your subject matter does not fit these categories, consider other IP forms (trademark, copyright). Use the USPTO IP Identifier to help choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand application pendency and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Know what application pendency means and how long the process may take: total pendency is the time from filing to issuance or abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for potentially lengthy timelines; consult USPTO estimates for 'How long might it take?' and factor pendency into business decisions and filing strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and plan for fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of the fees involved in filing and prosecuting a patent application and how they vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees depend on application type, actions taken during processing, and entity status; fees are required for examination but do not guarantee grant. Check fee schedules, consider anticipated prosecution costs, and explore fee discounts for qualifying independent inventors and small businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider hiring legal representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether to hire a registered patent attorney or agent to prepare and file the application and navigate USPTO procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparing and prosecuting a patent application requires knowledge of patent law and USPTO procedures; hiring counsel can assist with complex legal and procedural issues. If represented, USPTO will communicate only with your registered representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search prior art / public availability before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Search public records for inventions similar to yours because you generally cannot patent an invention that is already publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior public availability includes prior patents, printed publications, public use, on-sale activity, or other public disclosures; a published or patented U.S. patent application filed by another inventor before you filed can also prevent patentability. Use Patent Public Search and learn how to conduct thorough searches—plan to spend hours learning, searching, and evaluating results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and file a complete application
rubrics_metrics.description: File a complete patent application with all required parts, forms, and content for the appropriate patent type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can hire a registered patent attorney/agent or file on your own. If filing yourself, register as an eFiler (create a USPTO.gov account and complete identity verification) before using Patent Center. Consult the 'Applying for Patents' guide for required parts, form, and content. Missing parts may trigger a notice of missing parts and require action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify identity and register as an eFiler before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: All Patent Center users must verify their identity before filing to prevent fraud and ensure authorized access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start the one-time identity verification early so registration is complete when you are ready to file. Failure to register/verify will prevent filing via Patent Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work cooperatively and timely with the assigned patent examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: A USPTO patent examiner will review the application for compliance with legal requirements; applicants should respond timely and in writing to office actions and USPTO notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely written responses are essential; consider scheduling an interview with the examiner to discuss and resolve issues. If represented, the USPTO communicates only with the registered attorney/agent. Learn 'What happens during examination?' and how to respond to office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address rejections and know appeal options
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims are rejected during prosecution, follow the prescribed response and appeal procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any pending claim is rejected twice, you may file an appeal with the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB). Learn the procedures for responding to office actions and for appeals if prosecution does not resolve rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay Notice of Allowance and observe non-extendable deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is allowed, you will receive a Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due that must be paid within the specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must pay the fees shown on the Notice of Allowance within three months from the mailing date; this three-month period is not extendable. Failure to pay on time results in abandonment and no patent issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain issued patent and pay maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: After issuance, maintain the patent by timely paying required maintenance fees and monitoring patent term adjustments or extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term of a utility or plant patent generally lasts 20 years from the U.S. filing date, subject to payment of maintenance fees and any patent term extension, adjustment, or disclaimer. Use eGrants and Patent Center to access electronic patent grants and manage post-issuance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use USPTO resources and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage USPTO resources, services, and training to support searching, filing, examination, and maintenance activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO offers Patent Public Search, training on patent examination and quality, inventor chats, assistance programs for independent inventors and small businesses, and an Open Data Portal for USPTO data. Explore assistance resources (e.g., 'What if I receive a notice of missing parts?', 'Learn about patent initiatives') as needed.
